name: contract-first-execution
goal: Prove CLI-authored committed contracts drive server-created tasks; Codex reads app contracts without source discovery; Claude/Codex workers have app-wide contract reads and enforced assigned-file writes; validation rejects every missing mandatory field; automatic dispatch starts and records real workers.

title: Contracts can be authored through CLI with invalid-input atomic rejection.
Real child processes read all app contracts, edit assigned files, and are denied foreign writes and source/test discovery.
Server validates a desired-contract plan, creates tasks and starts real Claude/Codex workers without manual worker launches.
Active and generated Harness skills require contract-first CLI discovery and assigned implementation boundaries.
Global and scoped validation reject every missing mandatory metadata field while reporting evidence gaps separately.
Defining a wanted contract through the API creates a committed module task and the existing authorized project server dispatches it automatically; no separate manual worker command is required.
